claim: Nice's private beach clubs along Promenade des Anglais charge roughly €35 single-lounger / €85 double with umbrella at Beau Rivage, with Opera Plage at €30 incl. umbrella and Ruhl Plage at €90 for a double set.
quote: Plage Beau Rivage Nice — Single lounger €35 per day; Double sunbed with umbrella €85. Opera Beach — Daily lounge chair rentals are priced at €30 and include an umbrella. Ruhl Plage — Double sun lounger with an umbrella and towel €90.

claim: Budgeting for a Nice private beach day for two people typically runs at least €100 once sunbeds, lunch and drinks are tallied.
quote: for a private beach for 2, count on dropping a hunsky at a minimum: a sunbed is 20€-50€ per person… anything you order for lunch will be 20€, 7€ on average for a glass of rosé or a coke.

claim: The Cap Ferrat sentier littoral is a roughly 6–7 km coastal loop around the Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat peninsula taking a half-day, with some rocky exposed sections despite its easy reputation.
quote: the full loop is roughly 6–7 kilometers (about 3.5–4.5 miles), and most people walk it as a half-day activity… some sections of the trail are steeper and more exposed than you might expect, with long stretches of rocky terrain, very little shade.

claim: Paloma Beach sits at the end of the most picturesque eastern stretch of the Cap Ferrat coastal path, while Plage de Passable bookends the western side with a beach club, café and public space.
quote: the final section of the sentier du littoral leading up to Paloma Beach is truly the most adorable and charming section… Plage Passable, a smallish beach with a beach club, cafe, and some public beach space.

claim: Plage de la Mala in Cap d'Ail is a secluded cliff-backed cove reached only via a long staircase, which keeps crowds thin even in peak summer and where waters consistently rank as the region's cleanest.
quote: Plage Mala is one of the most stunning beaches on the Côte d'Azur, a secluded spot surrounded by cliffs in the small town of Cap d'Ail… consistently rank as the cleanest sea water in the region. Because access is only down a long flight of stairs, the beach is usually free of crowds.

claim: Plage de la Garoupe on Cap d'Antibes offers fine sand with crystal-clear water at the entrance of the cape's coastal path and is recognised as a top swimming spot.
quote: The sandy beach of La Garoupe, at the entrance to the authentic coastal path, is famous for its crystal-clear waters… stunning natural setting with fine sand mixed with a few pebbles and crystal-clear water.

claim: Plage des Marinières at Villefranche-sur-Mer stretches roughly 1 km with shallow, calm water that makes it a locals' favourite swimming beach near Nice.
quote: Plage des Marinières beach stretches around 1 km along the bay… Nice locals choose Plage des Marinieres as their go-to place for swimming in the calm waters, and the shallow drop-off is reassuring to families.

claim: Mercantour National Park trailheads sit roughly 90 minutes to two hours from Nice by car, with a direct scenic train option to La Brigue making day hikes feasible.
quote: Mercantour National Park is easily accessible by direct scenic train from Nice to La Brigue, or most hikers choose to drive a rental car to the mountain trailheads, with the journey usually taking between ninety minutes and two hours.

claim: Vallée des Merveilles holds over 40,000 Bronze-Age rock carvings and can only be visited inside the protected zone with an accredited guide on roughly 2-hour tours.
quote: The red-rock valley is home to more than 40,000 rock carvings of animals and weapons dating from the Bronze age… Europe's largest open-air museum, highly protected and only accessible with an accredited guide, with tours lasting about 2 hours.

claim: The Esterel massif is a coastal volcanic range whose rhyolite rocks give the cliffs their distinctive red colour, peaking at Mont Vinaigre (618 m).
quote: soil and rocks of volcanic origin composed mainly of rhyolite, which gives the hills a red color. The highest point of the massif is Mont Vinaigre (618 metres or 2,028 feet).

claim: The Corniche d'Or (Route de la Corniche d'Or, the N98) is a roughly 30 km coastal drive between Saint-Raphaël and Cannes hugging the red Esterel cliffs.
quote: The Corniche d'Or (literally "golden cornice") is a 18.6 mile (30 km) drive along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, from Saint Raphael to Cannes.

claim: Boat tours from Saint-Raphaël or Agay are the best way to see the Esterel's hidden calanques and sea caves inaccessible by land.
quote: For the most dramatic calanques, join a boat tour from Saint-Raphaël or Agay to get a whole new perspective on this dramatic section of coastline and access caves and secret coves that are impossible to reach by land.

claim: Horizon ferries run year-round from Cannes to Île Sainte-Marguerite roughly every 30 minutes between 9:00 and 17:30, with tickets from about €16 and a 15-minute crossing.
June on the Côte d'Azur typically delivers sea temperatures around 20 °C, daytime highs near 25 °C, and 10–12 hours of sunshine with only 20–30 mm of rain across ~4 days.
quote: the average sea temperature in June on the Côte d'Azur is around 20°C (68°F)… Maximum temperatures reach around 25°C (77°F)… You can expect around 10 to 12 hours of sunshine a day. Rainfall is generally low, with rainfall in Nice between 20 and 30 mm over 4 days on average.

claim: The Cap d'Ail sentier littoral runs roughly 3.6 km from Marquet Beach to Mala Beach and connects on to Monaco in about 1.5 hours total walking time.
quote: easy 3.6 km walk from Marquet beach, which opens onto the Principality of Monaco, to Mala beach… The walk to Monte Carlo (with the casino and Café de Paris) takes approximately 1.5 hours.

claim: The Mont Boron–Mont Alban loop above Nice is a moderately challenging hike averaging around 2 h 50 min with sweeping views over Nice, Villefranche bay and toward Cap Ferrat.
quote: a moderately challenging Mont Boron - Mont Alban route takes an average of 2 h 50 min to complete… sweeping panoramic views from the Cap Ferrat peninsula in the east all the way to the Esterel mountains in the west.

claim: Calanques National Park sits just outside Marseille and is best visited May–June, but its location west of Marseille places it many hours from Nice, making it impractical as a Nice-based weekend side trip.
quote: The best time to visit Calanques National Park is between May and June, with late spring/early summer weather being incredible… from June – September, reservations are required for some of the more popular areas.
